So here's the thing about cooking: everyone acts like it's this super complicated art form, but honestly? Most of it is just not burning stuff. That's like 80 percent of the job right there. Don't burn the garlic, don't burn the onions, don't walk away from the stove and forget you had something on it. We've all been there.

I've been trying to get better at it lately, and you know what's actually helped? Just tasting things as you go. Sounds obvious, right? But I spent years just following recipes blindly and wondering why everything came out kind of meh. Turns out you're supposed to actually check if it needs more salt!

The other thing nobody tells you is how much cleanup there is. Every cooking show makes it look so clean and easy. They've got their little bowls of pre-chopped everything, and someone's doing their dishes off-camera. Meanwhile, I've got every pot I own dirty and there's somehow flour on the ceiling. How did it get on the ceiling? I wasn't even using flour!

But when you nail a dish? When it actually turns out good? That feeling is unbeatable.
